PLACEHOLDER — replace this page entirely.
It exists to demonstrate three mechanisms you'll use constantly.

## 1. Linking to another page {#sec-linking}

Point links at the **source** file, not the compiled HTML:

> This builds on [Shared Methods](shared-methods.qmd), and connects to [Related Topic](related-topic.qmd).

Quarto rewrites `.qmd` to `.html` in the output.
The advantage of naming the source file is that Quarto checks it exists during the render — a typo becomes a build warning rather than a dead link a stranger finds later.

## 2. Cross-references

The heading above is tagged `{#sec-linking}`, so any page can point at it with `@sec-linking` and get an auto-numbered link with the correct title.
See @sec-code below for another.

## 3. Running R code {#sec-code}

Fenced blocks marked `{r}` are executed at render time, and their output is embedded in the page:

```{r}
#| label: demo-chunk
#| echo: true

x <- c(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42)
summary(x)
```

Chunk options go in `#|` comments at the top of the block.
Common ones: `echo: false` hides the code but keeps the output, `eval: false` shows the code without running it, `warning: false` suppresses warnings.

Because `freeze: auto` is set in `_quarto.yml`, this chunk re-runs only when this file changes, not on every site render.
